Ellis.feeling: Frustrating: I had the real Owl read and went all-in, then got winked before Finley could come over, and the table is drifting onto me.

Finley.feeling: This round is murky and tense: the table is piling onto Ellis, but his wink-death makes me suspect Alex.

Alex.note: Ellis already has 4 live votes and only Finley's 3 can go elsewhere, so Ellis goes. He's very likely Farm: he declined my bond and his Owl report looked genuine. Throwing both cards: the King banks 13 if Meowfia wins.

Blair.note: Thrown early, with the double down.

Casey.note: Thrown early, with the double down.

Ellis.note: Thrown early, with the double down.

Finley.note: Ellis gets eggsecuted either way (6 votes against my 3). Throwing at Alex banks everything if Farm wins, and returns C13 if Ellis was Farm and Alex a cat. So throwing at Alex is never worse.

Alex.confusing: The rules said at most 2 Meowfia, but rounds 2 and 3 each had three (me, Blair, Ellis, then me, Blair, Casey). Because I trusted that limit, I misread who my partners were and argued that Ellis's report was impossible.
Alex.fun: Round 3: Ellis was winked, so his 7-card double-down on me stopped counting as votes, and the vote turned around. Picking up bonds from everyone who would shake was satisfying too.
Alex.change: Make sure the Meowfia count follows the stated rules, or tell players the real maximum. Also make the Maine Coon's challenge more practical, since guessing every animal is almost impossible.
Alex.regret: In round 2 I threw all 6 cards at Blair after Ellis's last-second switch. Ellis wasn't my only partner: Blair was a cat too. If I had kept to my own call on Casey, Casey would have been eggsecuted and I'd have banked about 30.

Blair.confusing: The rules say at most 2 Meowfia per round, but rounds 2 and 3 each had three. In round 2 I trusted the limit, decided Ellis must be Farm and attacked a teammate. It was also unclear at first that a double down only goes through when you win the floor.
Blair.fun: In round 1, catching Ellis claiming my own role (Tit) and doubling down on him, then winking the real Owl in round 3 and still winning that round on a Turkey claim.
Blair.change: Either enforce the 2-Meowfia cap or state the real limit. Hidden-team logic depends on the count, and a wrong count punishes careful deduction.
Blair.regret: In round 2 my fake claim that I visited Ellis left exactly three Drew-visitors in the count, which outed me as the Floofer and got me eggsecuted. Knowing Ellis was a fellow cat, I'd have backed the push on Casey with everyone else instead. That likely wins the round, enough to make up the 2 points I lost by.

Casey.confusing: The rules say at most 2 Meowfia, but the hidden roles show 3 in rounds 2 and 3 (Alex, Blair, Ellis; then Alex, Blair, me). The Sphinx also listed only Kookaburra, Owl and Tit, which made me sure Alex's Hawk was a lie. I couldn't tell whether that list covered all Farm roles in play.
Casey.fun: In round 3 I doubled down on Ellis with a Falcon claim nobody could counter. Then I collected three handshake bonuses, including Finley's, to edge Blair by 2 points.
Casey.change: Have the Storyteller confirm each player's own nest count and clarify the Meowfia cap, since the rules and the hidden roles disagreed.
Casey.regret: In round 2 I trusted Blair, who was the Floofer, and backed Ellis instead of Blair. If I'd pressed Blair's unverified Tit claim, I'd have looked sharper, though Farm won either way.

Drew.confusing: The rules say at most 2 Meowfia per round, but the reveal shows 3 cats in rounds 2 and 3. The Maine Coon was in the pool with no description, so I couldn't explain my egg loss.
Drew.fun: In round 2, Alex and Casey both claimed Kookaburra while Finley's Owl report put three animals on me. It was satisfying to see that Ellis had to be a cat whichever Kookaburra was real.
Drew.change: Either enforce the stated Meowfia cap or announce that it can be exceeded, and print every pooled animal's ability, especially the Maine Coon's.
Drew.regret: In round 3 I went quiet after one line and didn't contest the CAW. I should have bid 3 to press that Ellis's Owl report needed Blair's Turkey claim to be a lie, and that Casey's Falcon story backed Ellis, not Casey's own push.

Ellis.confusing: The rules say at most 2 Meowfia per round, but rounds 2 and 3 each had three. The Maine Coon was also in the pool but never described, so I couldn't account for it when I reasoned about who visited whom.
Ellis.fun: In round 3, putting my Owl report together with the visit claims to name two cats, then getting winked right after, which showed I'd hit a nerve.
Ellis.change: Either enforce the cap on Meowfia or announce the possible counts, and give every animal in the pool a written description.
Ellis.regret: In round 3 I assumed Casey's claim to have seen me visit Drew was real and threw everything at Alex. Casey was the Sphinx and had simply guessed my visit; the Maine Coon wasn't on Drew's visitor list at all. I should have put Casey and Blair (Mouser) together and thrown only some cards, not my whole nest.

Finley.confusing: The rules say at most 2 Meowfia per round, but rounds 2 and 3 each had 3 cats. I reasoned from "two cats max" all game, so this one hurt. In round 3 that logic meant I trusted Casey's Falcon claim when Casey was actually a Sphinx.
Finley.fun: My round 2 Owl read on Drew was the most fun. Three visitors, two of them cats, set off a chain of claim-checking where each answer narrowed things down.
Finley.change: The cap on cats should be enforced as written, or the real number should be stated. Otherwise counting cats from egg changes and visitors, which is the core skill, is unreliable. I'd also make the handshake offers cost something, since cats used them freely to look trustworthy.
Finley.regret: I'd take back bonding with Casey, which cost me 3 points. I should have stayed suspicious of whoever pushed hardest against Ellis's Owl claim. I would also have doubled down on Alex early in round 3, before the table settled on Ellis.

review.title: Three Cats, One Wink
review.headline: Three winks, three dead truth-tellers, and a Sphinx wins by two points with handshakes.
review.summary: Farm won round 1 when the real Tit exposed Ellis's fake Tit claim. Round 2 was dealt three Meowfia, which the rules forbid. Alex then threw at his own partner and lost the cats the round on a coin-flip tie. In round 3 the engine again dealt three cats. Blair winked Ellis, the honest Owl, which voided his doubled 7-card vote. The cats eggsecuted him, and Casey's double down plus three handshakes lifted her from 30 to 71, edging Blair by 2.

rounds.recap: Ellis (Mouser) winked Drew the Owl before he could speak and claimed Tit. Blair, the real Tit, doubled down on Ellis at once. Casey and Finley worked out that Drew's Owl egg explained Ellis's +1, and Ellis was eggsecuted 17 votes to 7.

Finley's Owl report put Floofer, Kookaburra and Maine Coon on Drew. Alex's fake Kookaburra claim and Ellis's fake Hawk clear of Alex both broke against that count. Ellis winked Drew. The votes split 6 on Blair (all from her partner Alex) and 6 on Ellis, a tie between two Meowfia. The random pick took Blair, so Farm won.

Ellis's Owl report (Mouser, Sphinx, Tit on Drew) was true, and he doubled down 7 cards on Alex. Blair then winked him, so those votes stopped counting. The three cats' 6 votes on Ellis beat Finley's 3 on Alex, and Farm lost. Drew had been zeroed by a confused -2 report and could not throw at all.

highlights.text: Blair doubles down 5 cards on Ellis the moment Ellis claims Blair's own role, the Tit, and banks 34.
Ellis correctly outs Blair as the Floofer to save himself, and his partner Alex obeys and stacks 6 cards on his own teammate.
Casey invents a Falcon read that Ellis visited Drew, guesses right, and the honest Owl uses her lie as proof.
Blair winks Ellis just after his 7-card double down on Alex, which wipes out the only vote that could have beaten the cats.

confusions.what: Threw all 6 cards at Blair because Ellis's last message named her. His note assumed Ellis was also on Blair, but Ellis threw at Casey. That made the tie that lost the cats the round.
Rated Ellis 3% Meowfia from the 'at most 2 Meowfia' rule (Floofer plus Maine Coon already on Drew). The logic was sound, but the engine had dealt 3 cats, so the rule misled her.
Argued that Ellis's report meant three Meowfia, which the rules forbid. That was correct by the rules, but the engine had in fact dealt three.
Offered Casey a bond thinking she was Farm. She was the Sphinx, which cost Finley 3 points and gave Casey the margin of victory.
Claimed a Hawk visit to Alex even though Finley's public Owl list already had a Maine Coon on Drew. The lie could not survive the visitor count.

worked: Tit plus unique roles: a duplicate claim of a role that can only be dealt once is hard proof. It gave Blair a clean, confident double down in round 1.
Owl visitor lists: an animal list with no names forced every claim to fit a count. That made Ellis's lie in round 2 and Ellis's true report in round 3 checkable.
Crimson Kunzea created real all-in moments: Blair in round 1, Casey's 32-point swing in round 3, and Ellis's doubled bet that a wink cancelled.
Public throw counts with hidden values let players reason about vote math during the day, which drove several CAW calls.
problems: Setup bug: rounds 2 and 3 each dealt three Meowfia, which breaks the 'at most 2' rule. Players who reasoned correctly from the rule (Blair and Alex) were punished. Enforce the cap in the engine.

Maine Coon is in the pool but has no rules text. Alex held it all three rounds with no known ability. Add its text or remove it. Also, Alex was Meowfia every round and Ellis was the Mouser twice. Check the randomizer.

The Mouser's Wink is too strong. Every round a cat winked the best information holder (Drew, Drew, Ellis), and a dead player's double down stops counting as votes. Possible fixes: allow the wink only after half the talk, or let dead players' votes still count.

Golden Wattle always pays Meowfia +3, so cats accept every handshake and spam them (five bonds in round 3). That decided the winner. Accepting is close to a free tell, but it is also free points. Make same-team cat bonds pay less, or have both bonded players lose when their sides differ.

A confused Kookaburra really discards the fake loss. Drew went to 0 cards in round 3 and was locked out of voting and scoring. Make the confused egg count informational only, or apply it as a draw. Also strip engine leaks like 'no effect at tier 50' and the blank Sphinx target from the logs.
